extracted.intended_audience: chemical manufacturers and importers; employers; safety, health, and compliance professionals; regulators and hazard-communication practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory criteria for implementing and complying with OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard (29 CFR 1910.1200), including hazard classification, labeling, safety data sheets (SDSs), written programs, training, and related appendices for health and physical hazard criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose — the objectives of the HCS to provide standardized approach for communicating workplace hazards associated with exposure to hazardous chemicals, ensuring employees are apprised of chemical hazards, reducing occupational illnesses and injuries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that HCS requires classification of chemical hazards by manufacturers/importers and requires employers to provide hazard communication programs, labels, SDSs, information and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope and Application — which chemicals, industries, and activities are covered by 29 CFR 1910.1200 and the HCS revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies applicability across industries where workers are exposed to hazardous chemicals and notes the regulatory text organization by paragraph (purpose, scope, definitions, hazard classification, written program, labels, SDSs, trade secrets, dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions — required and clarified definitions of terms used in the HCS and the appendices (e.g., 'mixture', 'substance', hazard class/category, pictogram, SDS section names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes changes/clarifications to terms used throughout the standard; definitions affect classification, labeling, and SDS requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazard Classification (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hazard Classification — general criteria and approach for determining whether a chemical meets hazard class and category criteria under the HCS (alignment with GHS Rev. 7 where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framework used across Appendix A (health hazards) and Appendix B (physical hazards): tiered evaluation, available data, test methods, weight of evidence, and specific classification criteria per hazard class.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.0 General Classification Considerations — Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: A.0.1 Classification — overall approach to classifying substances and mixtures for health hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out that classification should rely on available data, appropriate tests, and weight-of-evidence; classification schemes and tiers are described in subsequent sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.0 — Available Data, Test Methods and Test Data Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: A.0.2 Available Data, Test Methods and Test Data Quality — consider the quality and relevance of data and test methods when classifying hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides evaluators to evaluate methodological quality and relevance of human, animal, in vitro, and other data sources when making classification decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.0 — Classification Based on Weight of Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A.0.3 Classification Based on Weight of Evidence — use weight-of-evidence integration when data are mixed or incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to weigh human, animal, mechanistic, and other data to reach a classification decision and when weight-of-evidence can modify classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.0 — Considerations for the Classification of Mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: A.0.4 Considerations for the Classification of Mixtures — principles for evaluating mixtures when full-mixture data are or are not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes tiered approach: prefer data on the complete mixture, then bridging principles, then cut-off values/concentration limits or additivity approaches when mixture data are lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.0 — Bridging Principles for the Classification of Mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: A.0.5 Bridging Principles for classification of mixtures where test data are not available for the complete mixture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies recognized bridging principles (e.g., dilution, concentration, interpolation within categories, aerosol conversions) to infer mixture hazard from ingredient data when complete mixture data are absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.1 Acute Toxicity — Definition and Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: A.1.1 Definition; A.1.2 Classification Criteria for Substances; A.1.3 Classification Criteria for Mixtures — criteria and tiered approach for acute toxicity classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes figure showing a tiered approach for mixtures: first-tier complete-mixture data, then bridging principles, then ingredient-based cutoffs/additivity; provides LD50/LC50 thresholds and rules for mixtures.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.2 Skin Corrosion/Irritation — Definitions and Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: A.2.1 Definitions and General Considerations; A.2.2 Classification Criteria for Substances (based on human data, animal data, in vitro/ex vivo data, other animal data, chemical properties, non-test methods, and a tiered approach); A.2.3 Classification Criteria for Mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how human clinical data, standard animal tests (skin corrosion vs irritation), validated in vitro methods, and non-test approaches may be used; includes tiered application and bridging for mixtures and a figure illustrating tiered approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.3 Serious Eye Damage/Eye Irritation — Definitions and Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: A.3.1 Definitions and General Considerations; A.3.2 Classification Criteria for Substances (including animal tests and tiered evaluation); A.3.3 Classification Criteria for Mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides tiered evaluation analogous to skin criteria; references figures for tiered evaluation and guidance on applying animal, in vitro, and other data.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.4 Respiratory or Skin Sensitization — Criteria and Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A.4.1 Definitions and General Considerations; A.4.2 Classification Criteria for Substances (separately for respiratory sensitizers and skin sensitizers, with hazard categories, human evidence, animal studies, and specific considerations); A.4.3 Classification Criteria for Mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines evidence standards for classifying respiratory sensitizers vs skin sensitizers, including human case reports, occupational studies, validated animal tests (e.g., LLNA), and special considerations (mechanistic, potency).

rubrics_metrics.name: A.5 Germ Cell Mutagenicity — Criteria and Tiering
rubrics_metrics.description: A.5.1 Definitions and General Considerations; A.5.2 Classification Criteria for Substances; A.5.3 Classification Criteria for Mixtures; A.5.4 Examples of Scientifically Validated Test Methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that, unlike many other health hazards, cut-off values/concentration limits are the primary tier for germ cell mutagenicity classification and that mixture classification may be modified case-by-case by available whole-mixture data; provides validated test method examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.6 Carcinogenicity — Definitions and Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: A.6.1 Definitions; A.6.2 Classification Criteria for Substances; A.6.3 Classification Criteria for Mixtures; A.6.4 Classification of Carcinogenicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides hazard categories for carcinogens, weight-of-evidence guidance, and cross-reference to IARC/NTP sources and non-mandatory guidance for applying external evaluative materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.7 Reproductive Toxicity — Criteria and Weight of Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A.7.1 Definitions and General Considerations; A.7.2 Classification Criteria for Substances (basis of classification, weight of evidence, maternal toxicity, animal/experimental data); A.7.3 Classification Criteria for Mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the use of animal developmental/reproductive studies, human data, and weight-of-evidence to assign reproductive toxicant categories and addresses lactation effects and categories for effects on or via lactation.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.8 Specific Target Organ Toxicity — Single Exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: A.8.1 Definitions and General Considerations; A.8.2 Classification Criteria for Substances (Category 1 and 2, and Category 3), including effects considered to support or not support classification and guidance values to assist classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides hazard category definitions, examples of effects supporting Category 1/2, narcotic effects criteria for Category 3, and guidance on using animal studies and guidance values.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.9 Specific Target Organ Toxicity — Repeated or Prolonged Exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: A.9.1 Definitions and General Considerations; A.9.2 Classification Criteria for Substances (hazard categories and guidance values); A.9.3 Classification Criteria for Mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out criteria, effects considered to support or not support classification, and tiered approaches for mixtures similar to other health hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: A.10 Aspiration Hazard
rubrics_metrics.description: A.10.1 Definitions and General Considerations; A.10.2 Classification Criteria for Substances; A.10.3 Classification Criteria for Mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines aspiration hazard, lists considerations (physicochemical properties, toxicological evidence), and gives rules for classifying substances and mixtures for aspiration risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix B — Physical Hazard Criteria (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix B provides definitions, classification criteria, and additional classification considerations for a comprehensive set of physical hazards (B.1–B.17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each hazard class in Appendix B has definitions, specific classification criteria, and additional considerations to align with GHS physical hazard classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.1 Explosives — Definitions and Classification Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: B.1.1 Definitions and General Considerations; B.1.2 Classification Criteria; B.1.3 Additional Classification Considerations for explosives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies hazard categories for explosives, required testing/criteria, and special considerations such as unstable explosives and desensitized explosives (see B.17).

rubrics_metrics.name: B.2 Flammable Gases — Definition and Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: B.2.1 Definition; B.2.2 Classification Criteria; B.2.3 Additional Classification Considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides flammable gas categories and criteria (e.g., flammability limits, energy of ignition), and considerations for testing and classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.3 Aerosols and Chemicals Under Pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: B.3.1 Aerosols (definition and classification criteria) and B.3.2 Chemicals Under Pressure (definition and classification criteria); plus additional classification considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines aerosols and compressed/liquified gases under pressure and specifies classification based on physical properties and hazards such as bursting or pressure release.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.4 Oxidizing Gases — Definition and Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: B.4.1 Definition; B.4.2 Classification Criteria; B.4.3 Additional Classification Considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets criteria for oxidizing gases, hazards related to supplying oxygen to combustion, and testing considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.5 Gases Under Pressure — Definition and Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: B.5.1 Definition; B.5.2 Classification Criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers compressed gases, liquefied gases, dissolved gases and refrigerated liquefied gases with classification based on pressure/temperature and physical hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.6 Flammable Liquids — Definition and Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: B.6.1 Definition; B.6.2 Classification Criteria; B.6.3 Additional Classification Considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides boiling point/flash point related criteria for flammable liquid categories and notes on special testing/mixture considerations (e.g., where boiling point unavailable use 10% distillation point per ASTM D-86).

rubrics_metrics.name: B.7 Flammable Solids — Definitions and Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: B.7.1 Definitions; B.7.2 Classification Criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers flammable solids and their hazard categories with criteria and additional considerations for classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.8 Self-Reactive Chemicals
rubrics_metrics.description: B.8.1 Definitions; B.8.2 Classification Criteria; B.8.3 Additional Classification Considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes self-reactive chemicals, test series, and classification criteria used to determine self-reactivity and hazard categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.9 Pyrophoric Liquids and B.10 Pyrophoric Solids
rubrics_metrics.description: B.9/B.10 Definitions and Classification Criteria for pyrophoric liquids and solids (ignite spontaneously in air).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets criteria and test requirements to determine pyrophoricity and assign hazard categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.11 Self-Heating Chemicals
rubrics_metrics.description: B.11.1 Definition; B.11.2 Classification Criteria; B.11.3 Additional Classification Considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines self-heating chemical hazards and prescribes classification criteria and tests for self-heating potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.12 Chemicals Which, in Contact With Water, Emit Flammable Gases
rubrics_metrics.description: B.12.1 Definition; B.12.2 Classification Criteria; B.12.3 Additional Classification Considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies criteria for substances that react with water to emit flammable gases and the hazard categories applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.13 Oxidizing Liquids and B.14 Oxidizing Solids
rubrics_metrics.description: B.13/B.14 Definitions and Classification Criteria for oxidizing liquids and solids, including additional classification considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines testing/criteria for oxidizing materials and how they are distinguished from non-oxidizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.15 Organic Peroxides
rubrics_metrics.description: B.15.1 Definition; B.15.2 Classification Criteria; B.15.3 Additional Classification Considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives specific classification rules for organic peroxides, including decomposition hazards, temperature sensitivity, and subdivision into types/categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.16 Corrosive to Metals
rubrics_metrics.description: B.16.1 Definition; B.16.2 Classification Criteria; B.16.3 Additional Classification Considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines and sets criteria for substances that cause corrosion to metals and related classification considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: B.17 Desensitized Explosives
rubrics_metrics.description: B.17.1 Definitions and General Considerations; B.17.2 Classification Criteria; B.17.3 Additional Classification Considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses explosives rendered less sensitive by phlegmatizers and provides criteria and testing (e.g., UN test series) for classification and communication on SDSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix C — Allocation of Label Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: C.1–C.4 Allocation of label elements including precedence of hazard information, hazard statement text, pictograms, precautionary statement text, supplementary hazard information, and requirements for signal words, hazard statements, pictograms, and precautionary statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how label elements are selected and combined, precedence rules when multiple hazards are present, required pictograms and signal words, text for hazard and precautionary statements, and design/placement considerations (figures included for hazard symbols).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence of Hazard Information on Labels
rubrics_metrics.description: C.2.1 Precedence of Hazard Information — how to prioritize and present multiple hazards on labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for which hazard statements/pictograms take precedence and how to arrange label content to avoid conflicting or duplicative statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazard Statement Text and Precautionary Statement Text
rubrics_metrics.description: C.2.2 Hazard Statement Text and C.2.4 Precautionary Statement Text — standardized wording for hazard and precautionary statements to be used on labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes mandatory and recommended text; examples and lists of precautionary statements (e.g., 'Wear protective equipment', 'Avoid contact during pregnancy') and guidance on changes to prevention and response columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictograms and Figures
rubrics_metrics.description: C.2.3 Pictograms — required pictograms, symbols and corresponding hazard classes; Figures C.1–C.2 demonstrate symbols (e.g., exclamation mark pictogram).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides required pictogram graphics and mapping between hazard classes and pictograms; guidance on where pictograms must be used on labels and SDSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Hazard Information
rubrics_metrics.description: C.3 Supplementary Hazard Information — optional/additional hazard information permitted on labels beyond core allocation elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when and how to include supplementary hazard info, clarifications, or additional statements that may aid safe use but are not part of the mandatory list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Signal Words, Hazard Statements, Pictograms, and Precautionary Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: C.4 Requirements for Signal Words, Hazard Statements, Pictograms, and Precautionary Statements — specific mandatory requirements for label text and elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details which signal words (e.g., 'Danger', 'Warning') must be used with particular hazard categories, and formatting and content rules for hazard/precautionary statements and pictograms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labels and Other Forms of Warning (paragraph f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels and Other Forms of Warning — regulatory provisions governing labels, small-container labeling, relabeling upon reclassification, and other warning forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes provisions for labels on very small containers, released-for-shipment labels, relabeling requirements, and compliance timelines; explains when abbreviated information may be used for very small containers (e.g., product identifier only).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) — Content and Required Sections (Appendix D and §1910.1200(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix D and section references set required SDS format and content, including Section 2: Hazard(s) Identification; Section 3: Composition/Information on Ingredients; Section 8: Exposure Controls/Personal Protection; Section 9: Physical and Chemical Properties; Section 10: Stability and Reactivity; Section 11: Toxicological Information; Section 14: Transport Information (nonmandatory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies mandatory SDS sections, the type of information each must contain, cross-references to label elements, and footnote guidance (e.g., when alternate calculations are used for storage purposes state it in Sections 7 and 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade Secrets (concentrations and ranges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade Secrets — provisions allowing claim of concentrations or concentration ranges as trade secrets and related required justification and disclosure rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details how and when chemical identity or concentration may be withheld as CBI, how to claim concentration ranges, the obligation to provide sufficient information for medical treatment, and agency procedures for confidential handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Hazard Communication Program (paragraph e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Written Hazard Communication Program — employers must develop and implement a written program describing how hazard communication requirements are met at the establishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program must describe labeling, SDS access, training for employees, methods to inform employees of hazards from non-routine tasks, and procedures for contractors; guidance addresses recordkeeping and program accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee Information and Training Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Information and Training — employers must provide information and training to employees on hazardous chemicals in their work area at the time of initial assignment and when new hazards are introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must cover interpretation of labels and SDSs, protective measures, and details of the written hazard communication program; OSHA provides timelines for compliance (e.g., phased compliance dates for mixtures and small-container labeling changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates / Compliance Deadlines and Incorporation by Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective dates, compliance timelines, and incorporation by reference — the final rule effective date and dates for incorporation by reference of certain publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule effective July 19, 2024; incorporation by reference approvals listed with dates; provisions include phased compliance periods for specific amendments (e.g., mixture-related updates within 3–3.5 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions to SDSs and Labels Due to Reclassification or Precautionary Statement Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for revising SDSs and labels when chemicals are reclassified, precautionary statements are revised, or concentration ranges change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies scope of required updates, whether relabeling of existing stock/containers is required, and the distinction between updated electronic files vs. physical relabeling for items released for shipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Very Small Container Labeling Provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Labeling for Very Small Containers — special provisions allowing minimum information (product identifier) on very small containers and associated unit cost savings rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes eligibility for abbreviated labeling, examples of small containers, estimated cost-savings, and comparison to more expensive label formats (pull-out, fold-back).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridging and Tiered Approaches for Mixture Classification (recurrent theme)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tiered approach for mixture classification across multiple hazard classes — preference for complete-mixture data, then bridging principles, then ingredient-based cutoffs and additivity rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated across health hazard appendices (A.1–A.10) and explicitly noted as not applying for some hazards (e.g., germ cell mutagenicity, certain cases for carcinogenicity/reproductive toxicity where cut-offs are primary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Non-test Methods and In Vitro/Ex Vivo Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable use of validated non-test methods and in vitro/ex vivo assays in classification decisions where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices describe circumstances where validated alternative methods (e.g., LLNA, selected OECD in vitro tests) may replace animal tests, and stress the need for scientific validation and professional judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence and Interaction With Other Agency Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Alignment and interaction with other U.S. agencies and international standards (GHS revisions, EPA, DOT, Health Canada, IARC/NTP), and how OSHA's HCS treats overlapping or differing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes rationale for aligning with GHS Rev.7, notes where OSHA declines to adopt certain GHS revisions, and explains coordination with agencies (e.g., transportation/labeling differences) and international partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix C — Changes to Precautionary and Response Columns (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of changes to the prevention column (wear PPE, avoid contact during pregnancy, do not handle until precautions read) and response column (rinse skin, get medical advice, remove to fresh air).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a non-exhaustive list of precautionary/response statement options and illustrates typical prevention and response instructions that must be considered in label/SDS text selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix D Footnotes and Nonmandatory Sections Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on nonmandatory items and footnotes in SDS sections (e.g., transport information nonmandatory; footnotes regarding alternate calculations and storage classifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when some SDS sections are nonmandatory, instructions for noting alternate calculations in Sections 7 and 9, and references to incorporated standards for tests/methods.
